chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nuḍr ibn Suwayd from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave under his ownership, so he divorced her with two divorces in accordance with the Sunnah, and she became separated from him; then he bought her back after that before she married another husband. He said: 'Is it not that ʿAlī (peace be upon him) ruled in this matter that one verse made her permissible and another made her forbidden, and I prohibit her for myself and my descendants?'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repurchasing a female slave after divorcing her with two divorces?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) references a precedent set by Imam Ali (AS) regarding a man who divorces his slave woman with two revocable divorces and then repurchases her. The Imam highlights a jurisprudential nuance where Ali (AS) deemed the transaction valid based on one verse but prohibited it for his own household based on another, illustrating the practical application of reconciling apparent Quranic contradictions in *fiqh al-ayat*. This case underscores the distinct legal status of slave women compared to free women in Shia jurisprudence, particularly concerning the *iddah* period and the right of repurchase.
